import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # Setup with mandatory lines
        title = "The Mechanism: The 'Shopping Cart' Analogy"
        lines = [
            'A shopping cart moves smoothly across the paved sidewalk.',
            'One front wheel hits the grass and slows down.',
            'This imbalance causes the entire cart to pivot.',
            'The cart now travels at a sharper new angle.',
            'Light waves bend exactly like this angled shopping cart.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Environment setup: Pavement (Rows A-C) and Grass (Rows D-F)
        pavement = Rectangle(width=6, height=3, fill_color="#AAAAAA", fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=0)
        grass = Rectangle(width=6, height=3, fill_color="#228B22", fill_opacity=0.4, stroke_width=0)
        self.place_in_area(pavement, 'A1', 'C6')
        self.place_in_area(grass, 'D1', 'F6')
        
        # Boundary line (between row C and D, roughly y = -0.3)
        boundary = Line(self.grid['C1'] + 0.5*DOWN, self.grid['C6'] + 0.5*DOWN, color=WHITE, stroke_opacity=0.5)
        self.add(pavement, grass, boundary)

        # Cart setup
        cart_body = Rectangle(width=0.8, height=1.2, fill_color="#808080", fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=1, stroke_color=WHITE)
        w_fl = Circle(radius=0.1, fill_color="#333333", fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=0).shift(0.3 * LEFT + 0.4 * UP)
        w_fr = Circle(radius=0.1, fill_color="#333333", fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=0).shift(0.3 * RIGHT + 0.4 * UP)
        w_bl = Circle(radius=0.1, fill_color="#333333", fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=0).shift(0.3 * LEFT + 0.4 * DOWN)
        w_br = Circle(radius=0.1, fill_color="#333333", fill_opacity=1, stroke_width=0).shift(0.3 * RIGHT + 0.4 * DOWN)
        cart = VGroup(cart_body, w_fl, w_fr, w_bl, w_br).rotate(-20 * DEGREES)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Resolved Issue 40/41/56: Position at B4, scale 0.6
        self.place_at_grid(cart, 'B4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(cart))
        self.play(cart.animate.shift(DOWN * 0.8 + RIGHT * 0.3), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Move until the front-right wheel hits the boundary
        # The wheel color changes to red to indicate friction/slowing down
        self.play(
            cart.animate.shift(DOWN * 0.4 + RIGHT * 0.15),
            w_fr.animate.set_color("#FF0000"),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Pivot the cart around the stuck wheel (w_fr)
        pivot_point = w_fr.get_center()
        self.play(
            Rotate(cart, angle=-25 * DEGREES, about_point=pivot_point),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Move the cart forward at the new angle
        # Heading direction is now deeper into the grass
        self.play(cart.animate.shift(DOWN * 1.0 + RIGHT * 0.1), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(cart))
        
        # Wavefronts: Horizontal-ish lines moving across the boundary
        # Resolved Issue 39/40/56: Position B4, scale 0.7 to avoid clipping and text crowding
        wavefronts = VGroup(*[
            Line(LEFT*1.8, RIGHT*1.8, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2).shift(UP*i*0.5).rotate(-20*DEGREES)
            for i in range(4)
        ])
        self.place_at_grid(wavefronts, 'B4', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # Prepare bent wavefronts to represent refraction
        bent_wavefronts = VGroup()
        for i in range(4):
            # Intersection point at boundary y=-0.3
            # We construct each bent wave as two segments
            top_seg = Line(self.grid['B4'] + UP*i*0.5 + LEFT*1.2, self.grid['C4'] + UP*i*0.5 + LEFT*0.2, color=WHITE).rotate(-20*DEGREES)

            bent_wavefronts.add(VGroup(top_seg, bottom_seg))

        self.play(FadeIn(wavefronts))
        self.play(wavefronts.animate.shift(DOWN * 1.5 + RIGHT * 0.5), run_time=2)
        
        # Transition to showing the bending effect
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(wavefronts, bent_wavefronts), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(2)
        
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)

sections.title: The Optical Illusion: The 'Broken' Pencil
sections.content: Introduce the phenomenon of refraction using a common visual anomaly. Define refraction as the change in direction of a wave passing from one medium to another, caused by its change in speed.
sections.example: A thirsty cartoon fox looks at a fish in a pond. To the fox, the fish appears shallower than it actually is because light 'bends' as it exits the water. The fox lunges at the 'apparent' position and misses.

sections.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: Speed and Optical Density
sections.content: Explain that light travels at different speeds in different materials. Introduce the 'Index of Refraction' (n = c/v). Use a visual scale showing that as 'n' increases, light speed 'v' decreases.
sections.example: Compare a marathon runner (light) moving on a clear paved road (vacuum/air) vs. the same runner moving through waist-deep water (glass/water). The runner naturally slows down due to the 'resistance' of the medium.

sections.title: The Mechanism: The 'Shopping Cart' Analogy
sections.content: Explain why speed changes cause bending. Use a top-down graphical view of wavefronts hitting a boundary at an angle. If one side of the wave slows down before the other, the entire path pivots.
sections.example: An animation of a shopping cart being pushed from a smooth sidewalk onto a patch of grass at an angle. The front-right wheel hits the grass first and slows down, causing the whole cart to pivot toward the grass side.

sections.title: The Math: Snell's Law and Geometry
sections.content: Introduce Snell's Law: n1 * sin(θ1) = n2 * sin(θ2). Use a split-screen visual: on one side, the equation; on the other, a dynamic ray diagram showing the 'Normal' line and how the angle shrinks when entering a denser medium.
sections.example: A laser beam (n1=1.0) hitting a block of glass (n2=1.5). An overlay shows a Protractor tool measuring the angle of incidence and the smaller angle of refraction, satisfying the ratio n2/n1.

sections.title: The Principle of Least Time: Fermat’s Logic
sections.content: Deepen comprehension by explaining *why* light chooses this specific path. Light always takes the path that requires the least amount of *time*, not the shortest distance.
sections.example: Leo the Lifeguard needs to rescue a swimmer. Instead of running in a straight line, Leo runs further along the fast sand and swims a shorter distance in the slow water to reach the swimmer in the minimum total time.

sections.title: Extreme Bending: Total Internal Reflection
sections.content: Demonstrate what happens when light moves from a dense medium to a less dense one at a steep angle. Introduce the 'Critical Angle' where light can no longer escape the medium.
sections.example: A fiber optic cable used in high-speed internet. Show a signal pulse 'bouncing' perfectly off the inner walls of the glass fiber like a ball in a tube, allowing data to travel across oceans without escaping the wire.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: A final 30-second recap linking the index of refraction, the change in speed, Snell's Law, and the practical applications in lenses and technology.
sections.example: A montage showing a camera lens (refraction), a diamond's sparkle (Total Internal Reflection), and the fox finally catching the fish by aiming slightly deeper.

storyboard.title: The Optical Illusion: The 'Broken' Pencil
lecture_lines: A fox sees a fish deep in the pond.
Light from the fish bends at the water's surface.
This creates an illusion, making the fish appear shallower.
animations: Draw a horizontal water surface (#1E90FF) with a fox icon (#D2691E) above and a fish icon (#FFD700) below.
Animate a light ray (#FFFF00) traveling from the fish to the surface and bending toward the fox's eye.
Draw a dashed ray (#FFFF00, opacity 0.5) extending straight back from the eye to a shallow, 'apparent' fish.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: Speed and Optical Density
lecture_lines: Light travels faster through air than through dense glass.
We see light slow down as it enters glass.
The index of refraction calculates this speed change.
animations: Show two light pulses (#FFFFFF) starting at the same x-position in Air (top) and Glass [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/glass.svg] (bottom, #E0FFFF).
The pulses move right; the pulse in Glass moves significantly slower than the one in Air.
Display the formula 'n = c / v' (#FFFFFF) and highlight the speed 'v' (#00FF00) as the pulses finish.

storyboard.title: The Mechanism: The 'Shopping Cart' Analogy
lecture_lines: A shopping cart moves smoothly across the paved sidewalk.
One front wheel hits the grass and slows down.
This imbalance causes the entire cart to pivot.
The cart now travels at a sharper new angle.
Light waves bend exactly like this angled shopping cart.
animations: Top-down view: A rectangular cart (#808080) with 4 wheels (#333333) moves diagonally on pavement (#AAAAAA).
The front-right wheel enters a green grass patch (#228B22), turns red (#FF0000), and slows down.
The cart's body rotates towards the grass side as the remaining wheels continue at original speed.
The cart continues through the grass at a steeper angle relative to the boundary normal.
Fade out cart; show parallel wave fronts (#FFFFFF) hitting the boundary and pivoting exactly like the cart.

storyboard.title: The Math: Snell's Law and Geometry
lecture_lines: Consider the boundary between air and dense glass.
A light ray hits the boundary near the normal.
Entering the glass, the ray bends toward the normal.
Snell's Law mathematically predicts this change in direction.
We measure these angles relative to the perpendicular normal.
animations: Draw a horizontal air-glass boundary (#FFFFFF); label Air (n=1.0) and Glass (n=1.5, #E0FFFF).
A red laser ray [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/laser.svg] (#FF0000) strikes the boundary; add a vertical dashed Normal line (#FFFFFF).
The ray bends toward the Normal inside the glass; label the Incident and Refracted angles.
Display Snell's Law: n1 * sin(theta1) = n2 * sin(theta2) (#FFFFFF) and color-code n1 and n2.
Overlay a semi-transparent protractor (#FFFFE0) to show the angle of refraction is smaller than the angle of incidence.

storyboard.title: The Principle of Least Time: Fermat’s Logic
lecture_lines: A lifeguard must reach a swimmer as fast as possible.
Multiple paths exist, but only one is the fastest.
The optimal path involves more running and less swimming.
This path minimizes total travel time to the swimmer.
Light follows Fermat’s Principle, taking the path of least time.
animations: Top half: Sand (#F4A460), Bottom half: Water (#1E90FF). Place Lifeguard at point A and Swimmer at point B.
Show three candidate paths: a straight line, a refracted-like path, and a 'too wide' path.
Highlight the refracted-like path (more sand travel, less water travel) in bright green (#00FF00).
Animate the lifeguard moving along all paths simultaneously; the green path reaches the swimmer first.
Label the green path 'Principle of Least Time' (#FFFFFF) and fade out the other sub-optimal paths.

storyboard.title: Extreme Bending: Total Internal Reflection
lecture_lines: Light inside glass hits the boundary at steep angles.
At the critical angle, light can no longer escape.
Total internal reflection keeps data trapped inside fiber cables.
animations: A light source inside a glass block (#E0FFFF) emits rays at increasing angles toward the air boundary.
As the angle increases, the refracted ray bends closer to the surface until it hits 90 degrees (Critical Angle).
Increase the angle further; the ray reflects perfectly back into the glass; show a pulse bouncing in a fiber optic cable (#FFFFFF) [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/fiber.svg].

storyboard.title: Summary and Synthesis
lecture_lines: Lenses use refraction to focus light into sharp images.
Total internal reflection gives diamonds their brilliant sparkle.
Understanding refraction helps the fox finally catch the fish.
animations: Show a convex lens (#E0FFFF) focusing incoming parallel light rays (#FFFFFF) to a single point.
Transition to a diamond shape (#B9F2FF) with internal light rays (#FFFFFF) reflecting and exiting with sparkle effects.

Final scene: The fox [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/fox.svg] (#D2691E) from Section 1 aims lower than the apparent fish [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/fish.svg] and successfully grabs it.
